question: The approximation of the steady state assumes that after the induction period the formation velocity is equal to the disappearance velocity for:

options.opd: All the species present in the reaction cell.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: The approximation of the steady state assumes -> after the induction period -> the formation velocity is equal to the disappearance velocity for -> the reaction intermediates -> 80% CHAIN: The approximation of the steady state assumes -> after the induction period -> the formation velocity is equal to the disappearance velocity for -> the reaction products -> 85% CHAIN: The approximation of the steady state assumes -> after the induction period -> the formation velocity is equal to the disappearance velocity for -> the catalyst of the reaction -> 75% CHAIN: The approximation of the steady state assumes -> after the induction period -> the formation velocity is equal to the disappearance velocity for -> all the species present in the reaction cell -> 80%
analysis: In the approximation of the steady state, the formation velocity being equal to the disappearance velocity implies a dynamic equilibrium where the rate of formation of products is equal to the rate of their disappearance. This applies to the reaction products.
